title: Custom SQL Pools for Fabric Data Warehouse (workload governance)
summary: Custom SQL Pools cap the maximum share of warehouse compute a workload can consume (application-name, application-name-regex, or statement-type classification), for workload ISOLATION and predictable resource usage — NOT a spending limit. Read the stable workspace-level config with 'warehouse get-sql-pools-config' and apply one with 'warehouse update-sql-pools-config'. Good candidates: ETL/data-loading, background processing, and Power BI reporting that must not starve other workloads. Under allocation-based billing, capping a bursty workload's peak allocation can indirectly reduce consumption (it runs longer at a lower vNode peak).
what_it_is: A governance boundary that limits the maximum percentage of warehouse resources a classified workload can access. Its primary purpose is workload isolation (keep a business-critical Power BI dashboard from contending with an aggressive ETL job); with allocation-based billing, governing allocation also affects consumption.
what_it_is_not: NOT a spending limit, monthly budget cap, or '$X/month maximum' — it does not stop charges after a threshold.
NOT a performance boost — it TRADES performance for a smaller/steadier resource footprint (a capped query may run longer at a lower peak).
good_candidates: ETL / data loading that cares about completion, not finishing a few minutes faster.
Power BI reporting you want to guarantee a fixed share so it cannot consume the whole warehouse during business hours.
Bursty workloads that frequently trigger the one-minute minimum allocation window — capping the scale peak can lower billed vNode-seconds.

config_shape.note: The stable GET/PATCH /workspaces/{ws}/warehouses/sqlPoolsConfiguration endpoint is workspace-scoped and governs all warehouses in the workspace. Classifier types are exact, case-sensitive API values: 'Application Name', 'Application Name Regex', and 'Statement Type'.
config_shape.toggle: customSQLPoolsEnabled (bool) turns the feature on/off; customSQLPools is the array of pool definitions.

recommended_workflow: 1. Build or capture a configuration using one of the documented classifier types: Application Name, Application Name Regex, or Statement Type.
2. Capture it as source-of-truth JSON: fabio warehouse get-sql-pools-config --workspace $WS --query . -o json > pools.json
3. Version pools.json in git and re-apply it to other workspaces/environments: fabio warehouse update-sql-pools-config --workspace $WS2 --file pools.json (use --dry-run first).
The GET → version → update pattern keeps the workspace-level configuration reproducible and auditable.
gotchas: The config is WORKSPACE-scoped (sqlPoolsConfiguration lives under /warehouses/, not a single warehouse id) — it governs all warehouses in the workspace.
Do not append ?beta=true; SQL Pools configuration now uses the stable endpoint.
Classifier type values are PascalCase-with-spaces and must be sent exactly: Application Name, Application Name Regex, or Statement Type.
Both read and update operations require the Admin workspace role.
see_also: Configure Custom SQL Pools in the Fabric Portal (Microsoft Learn)
